content:
Hi, working on a translation project we have this large file (~40k lines with several imports) encoding some basic arithmetic results in STT that makes Lean crash everytime is compiled via lake build. We have also tried ulimit -s unlimited and LEAN_NUM_THREADS=1 lake lean <file_name>.lean but we keep on getting the same stack overflow error. Sometimes it is able to compile 240 lines, sometimes less and sometimes a bit more but noting impressive.

The output from lake build:

info: stderr:
Stack overflow detected. Aborting.
error: Lean exited with code 134

vscode output:

Stack overflow detected. Aborting.
[Error - 2:03:50 PM] Request textDocument/inlayHint failed.
  Message: Server process for file:///....lean crashed, likely due to a stack overflow or a bug.
  Code: -32902

Stack overflow detected. Aborting.
[Error - 2:13:16 PM] Request textDocument/foldingRange failed.
  Message: Server process for file://...lean crashed, likely due to a stack overflow or a bug.
  Code: -32902
[Error - 2:13:16 PM] Request textDocument/semanticTokens/full failed.
  Message: Server process for file:///...lean crashed, likely due to a stack overflow or a bug.
  Code: -32902
[Error - 2:13:16 PM] Request textDocument/inlayHint failed.
  Message: Server process for file:///...lean crashed, likely due to a stack overflow or a bug.
  Code: -32902

I wish I could give you more details but the results are really basic, like just rfl tactics and building some terms.

For elaboration, the correct flag is --tstack=<size in Kb>. The error message has recently been adjusted on master to point this out. We are also planning to significantly increase the default stack size.
I also tried doing lake lean --tstack=n <lean_file> but it is not a valid flag, lean does not work because I need to check the file in the project context. Is there a similar option for lake?
It worked perfectly, thank you so much :)

Update and solution: to build the file (and the project) I had to add moreLeanArgs = ["--tstack=n"] to my lakefile.toml file since lean build was failing even after adding the suggested flag. Thanks again @Sebastian Ullrich . I have also opened an issue
